name: Insider Risk
description: Departing employees, privileged misuse and data theft by people with legitimate access. HR and Legal lead.

plays.title: Set up insider risk governance with HR and Legal
plays.summary: Agree in advance who can open an insider case, what monitoring is lawful, and who sees what.
steps: Write a charter naming the case owner, HR and Legal partners, and the approval needed to open a case
Check monitoring against employment and privacy law in each country, including works council agreements
Define need-to-know rules and a codename convention for cases
Decide how to handle a case involving security staff or executives

plays.title: Deploy lawful activity monitoring and DLP
plays.summary: Collect the signals you will need, within policy, before a case happens.
steps: Turn on DLP for USB, cloud sync, personal webmail and printing on managed devices
Log large downloads and sharing changes in SharePoint, Google Drive and code repositories
Feed HR events (resignations, terminations) to the insider risk tool through an agreed process
Tell employees about monitoring as the law and your policy require

plays.title: Open an insider case confidentially
plays.summary: Insider cases leak easily and can hurt an innocent employee. Keep the circle small from the first minute.
steps: Get the case approved as your charter requires and assign a codename
Limit the team to named people from Security, HR and Legal
Do not message the subject's manager or team until HR and Legal agree
Record the allegation, its source and the scope you are authorized to investigate

plays.title: Review data movement by a departing employee
plays.summary: Check whether someone leaving took data they should not have.
steps: Pull 90 days of activity before the resignation date and everything since
Look at USB writes, uploads to personal cloud storage, mail to personal addresses and printing
Look at bulk downloads from SharePoint, Drive, CRM and code repositories, and new repository clones
Compare against the person's normal baseline and their peers, not against zero
Hash and preserve anything you find

plays.title: Review privileged user misuse
plays.summary: An administrator may have used their access outside their job: snooping, sabotage, or creating access for later.
steps: Compare admin actions against change tickets for the period
Look for access to HR, executive or customer records with no business reason
Look for new accounts, keys, scheduled tasks or forwarding rules they created
Have someone outside the subject's team pull the logs

plays.title: Preserve the subject's data and devices
plays.summary: Place holds before anyone wipes, reissues or deprovisions anything.
steps: Place legal holds on the mailbox, OneDrive or Drive, chat and code accounts
Tell IT not to wipe or reissue the laptop and phone; collect them at return
Image the devices and log chain of custody
Hold badge, VPN and printer logs past their normal retention

plays.title: Interview the subject with HR and counsel
plays.summary: Interviews are HR-led and planned with counsel. Security supplies facts, not accusations.
steps: Prepare the evidence summary and the questions with HR and Legal
Decide the meeting time with access removal in mind
Have HR lead, with a witness present; follow local rules on representation
Record answers and any admissions or returned materials

plays.title: Remove access in step with HR
plays.summary: Remove every access path at the moment HR chooses, not before and not after.
steps: List every account: SSO, local, SaaS outside SSO, VPN, cloud consoles, code hosting, shared accounts
Disable them at the agreed time, revoke sessions and tokens, and collect hardware keys
Disable the badge and retrieve keys
Remove corporate data from personal devices with MDM selective wipe
Rotate shared passwords the person knew

plays.title: Recover data and get written certification
plays.summary: Get company data back and get a signed statement that no copies remain.
steps: Have counsel send a demand for return of company data
Collect devices and media containing company data
Where agreed, have a third party examine personal devices or accounts
Get a signed certification of deletion and non-retention

plays.title: Remove access the insider created
plays.summary: Find accounts, keys and automations the person left behind.
steps: Search for accounts, API tokens and SSH keys they created or that were issued to them
Remove mail forwarding rules, delegated access and shared-link grants they set up
Review scheduled tasks, cron jobs, CI pipelines and scripts they owned
Reassign ownership of systems they ran

plays.title: Assess and limit the business impact
plays.summary: Work out who is affected by the data that left and what you owe them.
steps: Classify the data: trade secrets, customer data, personal data, regulated data
With counsel, decide on notification, injunctions or law enforcement referral
Tell affected business owners and help them plan
Watch for the data turning up in competitors' products or online

plays.title: Close joiner-mover-leaver and least-privilege gaps
plays.summary: Most insider cases expose access nobody needed.
steps: Check how much of the subject's access was still needed for their job
Fix the offboarding steps that were slow or missed
Tighten DLP rules and alert thresholds using what you saw
Keep the review blameless and protect the subject's privacy in the write-up

templates.name: Departing employee data theft
templates.description: DLP or a manager raises concern that a leaver took sensitive data.
nodes: Concern about a leaver's data handling

templates.name: Privileged insider misuse
templates.description: An administrator is suspected of misusing access, from snooping to sabotage.
nodes: Immediate risk: counsel and HR approve removing access before the interview.
